title: Credential circuit, declarative retry templates, and async stream ergonomics across SDKs
author: Leah Park
release_notes: Introduces a lightweight credential circuit breaker across Py/TS/Go SDKs (fast-fail and cooldown), new declarative retry template support for common retry policies, ergonomic async stream helpers (peekable and cancelable iterables), and version bumps: py 0.15.0, ts 1.28.0, go 0.9.5. No breaking API changes; opt-in features behind flags.
description:
Motivation: We observed several customer patterns where transient auth failures (token service blips, rate-limited credential backends) caused long tail latency and repeated retry storms across SDK-backed streaming consumers. This PR introduces a compact, cross-SDK credential circuit primitive that short-circuits auth attempts after configurable failure thresholds, plus a declarative retry-template layer to make retry semantics auditable and portable. To improve developer ergonomics we add small async-stream utilities (peekable iterator, cancelable drain) that make common streaming patterns clearer and safer.

Summary of changes (single-string): Implement credential circuit middleware in Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs with the following behavior: track auth request failures per-credential key, trip when failure count + error types exceed policy, enter cooldown with exponentially increasing backoff and optional health-check probe. Add declarative retry-templates: YAML/JSON schema + runtime loader for common patterns (fast-fail, idempotent-retries, streaming-backoff) and static validators. Add async-stream helpers: peek() to preview next chunk without consuming, cancelableDrain() / drainWithTimeout() helpers that gracefully release KV caches and session heartbeats. Harmonize telemetry labels and metrics across SDKs for auth_circuit.status and retry.template.name. Add CI integration tests and small e2e scenario against a local credential-mock that simulates flapping token service. Bump package versions (py 0.15.0, ts 1.28.0, go 0.9.5) and update changelogs.

Checklist: [x] Design doc linked (ENG-2981) [x] Unit tests (auth/circuit, retry templates, stream helpers) [x] Integration test with credential-mock [x] Docs: examples and migration guide [x] Telemetry mapping defined [x] Version bumps and changelogs updated.

Compatibility notes: All changes are opt-in. Existing SDK users will see no behavioral change unless they enable the credential circuit (default: disabled) or load a retry-template. Where defaults were tightened we used conservative settings to avoid surprising production workloads. The async-stream helpers are additive and provided as small utilities—no existing iterators were mutated.

Rollout plan: Merge to main, deploy SDK package pre-releases for dogfood, enable credential-circuit in internal testbeds for 48h, then ship GA if telemetry stable. Rollback is straightforward via toggling the feature flag in SDK config or publishing a patch removing the opt-in flag.

testing: Unit test suites added for circuit logic (threshold, cooldown, probe). Integration suite uses credential-mock to simulate rapid flapping and verifies SDK behavior under load (streaming drains, kv-cache release). Manual dogfood: upgraded internal CLI and exercised streaming consumer for 24h. Backfills: added telemetry assertions to CI to prevent regressions in auth failure metrics.
upgrade_instructions: To opt in: pass credential_circuit: {enabled: true, threshold: 5, cooldown_ms: 60000} to SDK config, or load a retry-template via RetryTemplate.load('idempotent-fast-fail.yaml'). No other changes required. If unexpected short-circuits occur set enabled:false or tune threshold/cooldown. Refer to docs/sdk-feature-flags.md for examples per-language.
